title: Browser policy and Human+ relay preflight boundaries
pins: A consumer must not send a browser engine to an unconditional private-address refusal, revive a retired policy bypass through configuration, or let relay body text change an authorization/conflict status. All native DNS records must be checked before each relay HTTP leg; a positive response and a required trusted proxy must remain distinguishable from local preflight checks.
scope: Browser A14 and Human+ A13/A15 preflight/status slice using normally installed reviewed published releases. No connection-pinning or resolver-deadline claim.
construction: Native PHP Browser manager, relay endpoint and Guzzle transports; native TypeScript and Python policies and exchange. DNS APIs and injected HTTP are controlled at the existing seams. PHP concurrent cURL cases use a bounded disposable loopback server and real child process. Predictions were frozen before these adapters ran.
findings: Native observations from published artifacts agree and match independent expectations frozen before execution. Agreement cannot establish safety outside the predicted preflight/status boundary. Hosted PR, actual-main and normal-artifact evidence remain separate proof obligations.

discrimination.gap: Package production mutants are recorded separately. Canonical schema and artifact-provenance negative controls are enforced; actual hosted and main evidence have separate receipts.
